data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Malaysia factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Malaysia performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how performance relates to student background and school experiences. It reports descriptive benchmarks such as mean score trends (2012–2018–2022), proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and gaps by socio-economic status and gender. For example, Malaysia’s mathematics mean declined compared with 2018 and is below the OECD average; 41% reached at least Level 2 in mathematics (OECD average: 69%), while only 1% were top performers (Level 5/6). The factsheet also reports questionnaire-based indicators (belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement) and COVID-related learning experiences, but it does not present any predictive/ML modeling, model metrics, or an explicit PV/missing-data handling procedure in the provided text. Interpretation should therefore focus on descriptive comparisons and benchmark distributions rather than causal claims.
